originalText:
OGRE DIFFICULTY 50
Perception 7 (–3)
Defense 15, Health 45, Insanity 1d3, Corruption 1d3 + 1
Strength 15 (+5), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 9 (–1)
Descriptor Ogre, Size 2, Speed 10
Languages Trollish
Melee Attack—Morningstar Strength (+5) with 1 boon (3d6 +
2)
Devour The ogre can use an action to target one Size 1 or
smaller Defenseless or Unconscious creature in reach. It
picks up and eats the target, killing it instantly.
Vomit The ogre can use a triggered action when harmed
to spray semi-digested food from its mouth into a Size 3
space adjacent to its own space. Each object in the space
vulnerable to acids takes 3d6 damage. Each creature in the
space takes 1d6 damage and makes an Agility challenge
roll. On a failure, the creature takes 2d6 extra damage and
becomes Diseased for 1 minute. The ogre loses access to
this trait until it uses Devour or completes rest.

name: BOOGEYMAN

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Boogeyman
Life on the edges of the civilized lands is anything
but easy. Between the ordinary troubles one might
face—wild animals, blights, droughts, storms, and
the like—people must also contend with strange and
malevolent creatures stalking the nights, bent on
mischief and worse. One breed of ogre that has grown
large in the nightmares of children all over are the
boogeymen. These brutes have developed a taste for
the succulent flesh of children and go to great lengths
to feed their unspeakable hunger.
Boogeymen stand about ten feet tall and have thick
muscular bodies with heavy abdomens that descend
to about their knees. They have the heads of red-
furred lions with copper-colored eyes. Despite their
bulky forms, they move with surprising stealth when
infiltrating homes to snatch their favored meals from
their beds.
BOOGEYMAN DIFFICULTY 50
Perception 12 (+2); Darksight
Defense 16, Health 60, Insanity —, Corruption 1d3 + 1
Strength 16 (+6), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 11 (+1)
Descriptor Ogre, Size 2, Speed 12
Languages Common Tongue, Trollish
Frightening A creature not immune to the Frightened
affliction makes attack rolls against the boogeyman with 1
bane.
Silent A boogeyman makes no sound when it moves unless it
chooses to.
Melee Attack—Teeth Strength (+6) with 1 boon (3d6)
Attack Roll 20+ If the boogeyman has no swallowed
creature inside its space, a Size 1 or smaller target moves
into the boogeyman’s space—the boogeyman unhinges its
jaw and swallows the target whole.
The target has the Blinded, Deafened, and Immobilized
afflictions while swallowed. It moves whenever the
boogeyman moves to remain in its space. At the end
of each round, the target takes 2d6 damage from the
boogeyman’s digestive juices. A swallowed target
can attack the boogeyman from inside its space. The
boogeyman’s gullet has Defense 10.
When the boogeyman’s damage total equals its Health
score, it vomits any creature it has swallowed along with
the remains of other creatures. All fall into a heap inside a
Size 2 space adjacent to the boogeyman’s space.
Stinking Mist The boogeyman can use an action to turn into
a cloud of stinking mist until the end of its turn. The cloud
fills its space with partial obscurement. While in this form,
the boogeyman ignores damage from all sources, moves
by flying, and can pass through spaces wide enough to
permit the passage of air as well as spaces occupied by
other creatures. Any breathing creature that enters the
boogeyman’s space makes a Will challenge roll. On a
failure, the creature becomes Diseased until the end of its
next turn.

---

name: ETTIN

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Ettin
Ettins are ogres born with two heads and are common
enough that most people consider them a breed apart;
ettins who mate with other ettins or ogres, however,
always have ettin offspring. Ettins resemble ogres in
size and stature, and each head usually has its own
neck. There are some ettins who have two faces on
one overlarge, misshapen head, or have their second
head emerging from an unusual place in their bodies,
but these are few and far between.
With a second head comes a second personality,
and each head has its own distinct voice and manner
of speaking. Ettins are famous for bickering with
themselves, arguing over what to do or whom to
attack, often getting distracted enough to allow their
enemies to slip away. Conflicting desires can prevent
ettins from getting much done, but when they do
reach an accord, they pursue their goals with an
almost single-minded dedication.
ETTIN DIFFICULTY 100
Perception 10 (+0)
Defense 15, Health 80, Insanity 1d3 + 1, Corruption 1d3 + 1
Strength 15 (+5), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 7 (–3), Will 9 (–1)
Descriptor Ogre, Size 2, Speed 10
Languages Trollish
Immune Dazed, Stunned
Two Heads The ettin increases the number of actions and
triggered actions it can use in a round by 1. The ettin loses
access to this trait while injured.
Melee Attack—Flail Strength (+5) with 1 boon (3d6 + 2)
Devour The ettin can use an action to target one Size 1 or
smaller Defenseless or Unconscious creature in reach. It
picks up and eats the target, killing it instantly.
Vomit The ettin can use a triggered action when harmed to
spray semi-digested food from one if its mouth into a Size
3 space adjacent to its own space. Each object in the space
vulnerable to acids takes 2d6 damage. Each creature in the
space takes 1d6 damage and makes an Agility challenge
roll. On a failure, the creature takes 1d6 extra damage.
The ettin loses access to this trait until it uses Devour or
completes rest.

name: HORNED OGRE

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Horned Ogre
The trolls’ flirtation with the Void’s dark forces in the
practice of their magic stained both the world and the
foul creations the trolls made to live in it. Ogres and
giants walk in the Demon Lord’s shadow and thus
attract all kinds of demonic attention. This attention
transforms them, elevating them above their simple-
minded hunger to true cunning and pure evil. Among
the transformed can be found the horned ogres,
creatures who dwarf their kin both in terms of stature
and brutality.
Horned ogres dwell in places stained by the Void,
making their homes in ruined cities, crumbling
fortresses, or landscapes warped by the Demon
Lord’s fell influence. There, they attract other beings
enthralled by the Hunger in the Void to serve them,
from beastmen and cultists to monsters and other
abominations, all heaving and lurching from the
shadows to lend their might to whatever dread
purpose their dark lord demands. While horned ogres
might bow to more powerful masters, within their
own realms they rule as absolute tyrants over the
lesser creatures drawn there, obeying their masters in
a never-ending fear of being snatched up and eaten.
HORNED OGRE DIFFICULTY 250
Perception 11 (+1); Darksight
Defense 14, Health 120, Insanity —, Corruption 1d3 + 1
Strength 18 (+8), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 8 (–2), Will 12 (+2)
Descriptor Ogre, Size 3, Speed 12
Languages Common Tongue, Trollish
Frightening A creature not immune to the Frightened
affliction makes attack rolls against the horned ogre with 1
bane.
Ferocious When the horned ogre’s damage total equals its
Health score, roll a d6. On a 5 or 6, the monster heals 6d6
damage and then loses access to this trait for 24 hours
Melee Attack—Hammer Strength (+8) with 2 boons (4d6 + 6)
Attack Roll 20+ A target creature becomes Dazed until the
end of its next turn.
Melee Attack—Long Blade Strength (+8) with 2 boons (3d6
+ 6)
Cruelest Cut A Dazed, Defenseless, or Stunned target
takes 2d6 extra damage.
Two Attacks The horned ogre can use an action to make a
Hammer attack and a Long Blade attack.
Devour The horned ogre can use an action to target one Size
2 or smaller Defenseless or Unconscious creature in reach.
It picks up and eats the target, killing it instantly.
Vomit The horned ogre can use a triggered action when
harmed to spray semi-digested food from one if its mouth
into a Size 6 space adjacent to its own space. Each object
in the space vulnerable to acids takes 2d6 damage. Each
creature in the space takes 2d6 damage and makes an
Agility challenge roll. On a failure, the creature takes 2d6
extra damage. The horned ogre loses access to this trait
until it uses Devour or completes rest.
Oubliette Hammer
Some horned ogres carry hammers with a head
large enough to capture and contain a creature.
When the horned ogre has a Size 1 or smaller
creature Grabbed, the ogre can use an action to
stuff it inside the hammer. Make a Strength attack
roll against the target’s Strength. On a success,
the horned ogre locks the creature inside where it
remains until released. Any creature that can reach
the hammer while it’s not being held or carried
by the ogre can use an action to open the door.
A creature trapped inside the hammer’s head
cannot perceive beyond it and has total cover from
everything outside the hammer.
When the horned ogre makes an attack with its
hammer, the creature inside it takes 2d6 damage
and makes an Agility challenge roll. On a failure, the
creature takes 2d6 extra damage.

name: ONI

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Oni
The forests of Balgrendia conceal many terrible
things, horrors most people in the comparatively
civilized north cannot conceive. For the average
Balgrendian, these monstrous threats are just another
part of living at the edge of civilization. The ogres of
Balgrendia, called oni by the locals, do not suffer from
the stupidity or slavish hunger of their lesser kin.
Rather, the oni are cunning and crafty, but thoroughly

---

debased and wicked, eagerly spreading misery,
disease, and other unpleasantness wherever they can.
Some believe the oni descend from the first ogres
created by the trolls, while other tales recount the acts
of ogres cunning enough to kill and eat the trolls who
created them, thus gaining their power.
Oni stand about ten feet tall and weigh upwards
of eight hundred pounds. They have exaggerated,
hideous features, with mouths stretched wide into
frightening grimaces under black, glassy eyes. They
have two great, smooth horns breaking from their
brows, extending another two feet from their heads.
Most display some strange mutation, with extra eyes
or digits being most common. Their skin tone also
runs the gamut, with most being color of midnight or
that of hot coals. They carry iron clubs and gird their
loins with animal skins.
ONI DIFFICULTY 250
Perception 15 (+5); Darksight
Defense 17, Health 160, Insanity —, Corruption 1d3 + 2
Strength 17 (+7), Agility 12 (+2), Intellect 13 (+3), Will 12 (+2)
Descriptor Ogre, Size 2, Speed 12
Languages Common Tongue, Dark Speech, Trollish
Immune damage from disease; Diseased
Frightening A creature not immune to the Frightened
affliction makes attack rolls against the oni with 1 bane.
Disastrous Presence At the end of the round, each creature
within short range of the oni makes a Will challenge roll
with 1 bane. Ogres and creatures immune to Insanity ignore
this effect. On a failure, the creature becomes Impaired
until the end of the next round. If the creature has this
affliction already, it instead gains 1 Insanity.
Melee Attack—Iron Club Strength (+7) with 1 boon (4d6)
Melee Attack—Claw Strength (+7) with 1 boon (2d6)
Two Attacks The oni can use an action to make two melee
attacks.
Devour The oni can use an action to target one Size 1 or
smaller Defenseless or Unconscious creature in reach. It
picks up and eats the target, killing it instantly.
Plague Curse The oni can use an action, or a triggered action
in its turn, to target one creature within short range. Make
an Intellect attack roll against the target’s Strength score.
On a success, the target takes 1d6 damage and becomes
Diseased for 1 hour. Anyone the affected target touches
becomes Diseased for 1 hour. A creature with this affliction
takes 1d6 extra damage whenever it takes damage and
heals no damage.
Disappear The oni can use an action, or a triggered action
on its turn, to become invisible for 1 minute. The effect
ends early if the oni takes damage. The oni can use this
magical talent three times. It regains expended uses when
it completes a rest.
Change Shape The oni can use an action, or a triggered
action on its turn, to assume a Size 1 humanoid form with
any appearance it chooses. The oni can remain in this form
indefinitely; ending it requires no action. While in this form,
the oni loses access to its Frightening and Devour traits,
Disappear, and its Claw attack.
Unlike other ogres, oni possess an assortment of
supernatural abilities that help them infiltrate their
victims’ communities. Some stalk their prey invisibly,
or alter their physical forms to resemble someone
they killed and ate to deceive and then feast upon the
other members of their victim’s families. The mere
presence of an oni in a community is dangerous to
everyone who lives there, for these brutes also spread
disease and misfortune wherever they linger.

evidence.excerpt:
Oni
The forests of Balgrendia conceal many terrible
things, horrors most people in the comparatively
civilized north cannot conceive. For the average
Balgrendian, these monstrous threats are just another
part of living at the edge of civilization. The ogres of
Balgrendia, called oni by the locals, do not suffer from
the stupidity or slavish hunger of their lesser kin.
Rather, the oni are cunning and crafty, but thoroughly

---

debased and wicked, eagerly spreading misery,
disease, and other unpleasantness wherever they can.
Some believe the oni descend from the first ogres
created by the trolls, while other tales recount the acts
of ogres cunning enough to kill and eat the trolls who
created them, thus gaining their power.
Oni stand about ten feet tall and weigh upwards
of eight hundred pounds. They have exaggerated,
hideous features, with mouths stretched wide into
frightening grimaces under black, glassy eyes. They
have two great, smooth horns breaking from their
brows, extending another two feet from their heads.
Most display some strange mutation, with extra eyes
or digits being most common. Their skin tone also
runs the gamut, with most being color of midnight or
that of hot coals. They carry iron clubs and gird their
loins with animal skins.

name: STALLO

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Stallo
In stark contrast to the deadly cunning and
wickedness of the onis are the stallos. Gigantic ogres
of staggering stupidity, they haunt the frozen wastes
where they gorge themselves on seals, seabirds, and
the occasional traveler upon which they happen.
Stallos have nearly died out several times over the
centuries, but somehow a small population of them
endures across the wastes and into Blötland.
A typical stallo stands about 20 feet tall and weighs
several tons. It usually has bluish-white skin, with red-
rimmed eyes, and profuse body hair. It also has a great
sagging gut into which it stuffs whatever it can fit into
its cavernous maw.
Stallos know a few words of Trollish, but they prefer
to grunt instead of forming words.
STALLO DIFFICULTY 100
Perception 8 (–2)
Defense 13, Health 80, Insanity —, Corruption 1d3 + 1
Strength 18 (+8), Agility 8 (–2), Intellect 6 (–4), Will 9 (–1)
Descriptor Ogre, Size 4, Speed 10
Languages understands Trollish
Inured to Cold A stallo takes half damage from cold and ice.
Stupidity A stallo makes Intellect attack rolls and challenge
rolls with 1 bane. Creatures make attack rolls against its
Intellect with 1 boon.
Melee Attack—Teeth Strength (+8) (6d6)
Attack Roll 20+ If the stallo has no swallowed creature
inside its space, a Size 2 or smaller target moves into the
stallo’s space.
The target has the Blinded, Deafened, and Immobilized
afflictions while swallowed. It moves whenever the stallo
moves to remain in its space. At the end of each round, the
target takes 3d6 damage from the stallo’s digestive juices.
A swallowed target can attack the stallo from inside its
space. The stallo’s gullet has Defense 10.
When the stallo’s damage total equals its Health score,
it vomits any creature it has swallowed along with the
remains of other creatures. All fall into a heap inside a Size
4 space adjacent to the stallo’s space.
Melee Attack—Fists Strength (+8) (3d6)
Two Attacks The stallo can use an action to make a Teeth
attack and a Fists attack.
Devour The stallo can use an action to target one Size 2 or
smaller Defenseless or Unconscious creature in reach. It
picks up and eats the target, killing it instantly.

---

name: VODYANOY

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Vodyanoy
On the edge of the wilderness, whenever a dam bursts
and floods farmlands, or a mill’s waterwheel breaks
and falls, or a strong swimmer inexplicably drowns,
people blame the vodyanoy, a creature believed to be
an evil water spirit or faerie that hates all living things
that dwell on the land. While these tales are correct
in portraying the vodyanoy as hateful and malevolent,
it is most definitely not a faerie. Rather, it is a rare
breed of ogre, perhaps cursed long ago by faerie
magic, condemned to live in the bogs, lakes, and rivers
scattered across the wilderness.
To look upon a vodyanoy is to know its evil. It
resembles a naked old man with long hair and a thick
green beard clumped with algae, slime, and pieces
of dead fish. It has the facial features of a frog, but
with red eyes that burn like hot coals. Although the
vodyanoy is an excellent swimmer, it prefers to float
about on a half-sunken log, its limbs dangling in the
water, sometimes lazily paddling, as it watches the
shores through slitted eyes for any sign of prey.
While the vodyanoy is smaller than a regular ogre
and far more intelligent, it shares the same driving
hunger of its land-dwelling kin. It likes nothing better
than to get its webbed paws on a nice fat child or
halfling—both succulent, and easier to subdue than
larger folk.
A vodyanoy doesn’t court trouble, but it can’t go too
long without eating—it will often work mischief upon
a nearby community to lure larger victims into its
clutches, or to cause enough confusion so it can slip
in and grab an unguarded child. The vodyanoy can
cast water-based spells, using its magic to harass and
drown its victims.
VODYANOY DIFFICULTY 50
Perception 13 (+3); Darksight
Defense 16, Health 40, Insanity —, Corruption 1d6 + 1
Strength 14 (+4), Agility 11 (+1), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 12 (+2)
Descriptor Ogre (Aquatic), Size 1, Speed 10 (Swimmer)
Languages Common Tongue, Trollish
Horrifying A creature not immune to the Frightened affliction
makes attack rolls against the vodyanoy with 1 bane.
In addition, when a creature starts it turn with line of
sight to the vodyanoy, the creature makes a Will challenge
roll. A creature immune to the Frightened affliction ignores
this effect. On a success, the creature becomes immune
to this trait for 1 minute. On a failure, the creature gains 1
Insanity.
Melee Attack—Paws Strength (+5) with 1 boon (2d6)
Drown A target creature makes a Strength challenge roll.
On a failure, its lungs fill with water and cause it to become
Dazed. The target can use a triggered action on its turn to
repeat the challenge roll. On a success, the affliction ends.
On a failure, the target takes 1d6 damage.
Melee Attack—Tail Strength (+5) with 1 boon (1d6)
Attack Roll 20+ The target falls Prone.
Mind Ravage The vodyanoy can use an action to target one
creature it can see within medium range. Make a Will attack
roll with 1 boon against the target’s Intellect. On a success,
the target becomes Compelled for 1 minute. The vodyanoy
loses access to this talent for 1 minute.
Devour The vodyanoy can use an action to target one Size
1/2 or smaller Defenseless or Unconscious creature in
reach. It picks up and eats the target, killing it instantly.
Vomit The vodyanoy can use a triggered action when
harmed to spray semi-digested food from its mouth into
a Size 2 space adjacent to its own space. Each object in
the space vulnerable to acids takes 2d6 damage. Each
creature in the space takes 1d6 damage and makes an
Agility challenge roll. On a failure, the creature takes 1d6
extra damage. The vodyanoy loses access to this trait until
it uses Devour or completes rest.
